variants.title: Single slit with a helium-neon laser (632.8 nm)
variants.unknown: the width of the slit, measured with red He-Ne light
variants.note: 632.8 nm is the red line of the helium-neon laser, the standard laboratory source: its wavelength is known to a far better accuracy than this experiment needs, which is why the slit width can be worked out from it.

source.title: Helium-neon laser, principal red line at 632.8 nm (vacuum wavelength 632.991 nm)

variants.title: Single slit with a green laser (532 nm)
variants.unknown: the width of the slit, measured with green light
variants.note: 532 nm is the frequency-doubled line of a neodymium DPSS laser. Shorter waves bend less, so the same slit gives a narrower pattern than red light does.

source.title: Nd:YVO4 / Nd:YAG diode-pumped laser, frequency-doubled 1064 nm line at 532 nm
